research_insight_text_link.research_insight_description: Corvus Robotics is engaged in developing a method and system for drone localization and planning, focusing on a localization and flight planning system for drones performing inventory management in warehouses. This includes drones equipped with sensors, machine-learned models, and controllers to scan inventory items. The company is also working on data transfer and power delivery for robots via direct contact with docking stations, utilizing standard network protocols. These efforts address drone navigation, inventory scanning, and efficient robot charging.

overview_description.description:
Corvus Robotics is an autonomous inventory intelligence company building AI-powered drones and material handling equipment sensors for the world's largest warehouses and distribution centers. Its flagship product, Corvus One, is an autonomous inventory drone that performs continuous cycle counts and delivers real-time inventory visibility without operators, Wi-Fi, localization markers, or GPS. Corvus Trident brings the same intelligence to forklifts and material handling equipment through the company's AIMS (autonomous inventory management system) platform.

Corvus drones navigate GPS-denied warehouse environments using vision alone, reading existing barcodes day or night in fully lights-out facilities. The Corvus One for Cold Chain variant operates continuously in freezer environments down to -20°F, where manual counting is slow and hazardous. The system integrates with existing Warehouse Management Systems and deploys in weeks without facility downtime.

Founded in 2017 at MIT and headquartered in Mountain View, California, Corvus Robotics is trusted by Fortune 500 and Global 2000 enterprises across retail, manufacturing, logistics, and distribution.

product.name: Corvus One
product.description: An autonomous inventory management system that uses indoor drones, computer vision, and AI to perform pallet-level cycle counts and identify inventory discrepancies in warehouses.

product.name: Corvus One for Cold Chain
product.description: A cold-rated autonomous inventory drone system for freezer and cold-storage facilities, providing inventory counts and barcode or label scanning at temperatures down to -20°F.

product.name: AIMS (Autonomous Inventory Management System)
product.description: Software that consolidates inventory data from Corvus drones and forklift sensors into a searchable operational record for discrepancy management, planning, and warehouse analysis.

product.name: Corvus Trident
product.description: An AI-enabled forklift and reach-truck system that records pallet movements from inbound through outbound and provides real-time inventory-in-motion data through the AIMS platform.

product.name: Deployment and Implementation Services
product.description: On-site deployment, warehouse mapping, system configuration, WMS integration, and ongoing customer support for Corvus autonomous inventory solutions.

product.name: Corvus One for Cold Chain
product.description: An autonomous inventory robot for continuous inventory monitoring from ambient conditions through deep-freeze environments.
